candidates.description: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale used to assess how a patient's disease affects their daily living abilities.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the ECOG performance status value documented in the assessment or clinical progress notes.
candidates.measurement_definition: A categorical scale from 0 (fully active) to 5 (dead), where 0 represents a patient who is fully active, 2 represents an ambulatory patient capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities, and 3 represents a patient with limited self-care and is confined to a bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.
candidates.name: ECOG performance status
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence does not specify if the reported status is always the baseline or if it fluctuates during follow-up.

candidates.description: A quantitative measure of a patient's lifetime exposure to tobacco smoke.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the number of pack-years documented in the Social History section. If described as 'never smoker', value is 0.
candidates.measurement_definition: Calculated as the number of cigarettes smoked per day divided by 20 (to get packs), multiplied by the number of years smoked. Value is expressed in pack-years.
candidates.name: Smoking history (pack-years)
candidates.uncertainty: Some records list only pack-years without clarifying the exact duration of smoking or duration of abstinence.

limitations: The sample size is small, consisting of a limited number of patient records.
Smoking history is reported inconsistently (some as 'never', others as specific pack-years).
The evidence is limited to thoracic oncology patients, potentially introducing selection bias.
summary: The provided evidence identifies variations in baseline functional status and smoking history among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), spanning different histological types (adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma) and disease stages (Stage IIA to Stage IV).
